title: 3. Database tables and normalization
description: Insertion, update and deletion anomalies; 1NF, 2NF and 3NF using the lecture’s player-inventory example.

items.question: Alex moves to Sunway but only his Physics row is updated. What anomaly does this create?
items.explanation: Alex’s move from Lumut to Sunway must be recorded in all three rows. Updating just one leaves conflicting addresses.

context.title: Combined student–subject table — excerpt from the practical

items.question: The only way to record a new subject and its credit value in this design is to record a student enrolment. What anomaly is this?
items.explanation: The practical’s combined table has no independent place to record a new subject and its credits before anyone enrols.

context.title: Combined student–subject table — excerpt from the practical

items.question: Adam is the only student taking Computer. Deleting his enrolment also deletes the only record of its credit value. What anomaly is this?
items.explanation: Adam’s row was the only record of the Computer subject’s credit value. Deleting the enrolment deletes that fact too.

context.title: Combined student–subject table — excerpt from the practical

items.question: How does the lecture represent these inventory items in 1NF?

options.text: Store an item list in one cell
Use a separate row for each player–item pair
Add a numbered column for every item
Sort the values inside each cell

items.explanation: The slide puts Adam91’s arrows and rings in separate rows, with a single item and quantity in each row.

references.label: Week 5 normalization, p. 17
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 5 - Normalization of Database Table  28 Oct 26.pdf

context.title: Before 1NF — repeating inventory items
context.content: Adam91 has 2 arrows and 4 rings. Suppose both item–quantity pairs are listed together in one player record.

items.question: In the player inventory example, which attribute alone determines Player_rating?
items.explanation: Player_rating is determined by Player_Id alone, which is only one part of the composite key.

references.label: Week 5 normalization, p. 24
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 5 - Normalization of Database Table  28 Oct 26.pdf

items.question: Each row records a quantity for one player and one item. Which dependency uses the entire primary key to determine Quantity?
items.explanation: Quantity depends on both the player and item: Adam91 has 2 arrows but 4 rings, and another player may have a different quantity of arrows.

references.label: Week 5 normalization, p. 24
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 5 - Normalization of Database Table  28 Oct 26.pdf

items.question: The inventory table has single values in its cells and primary key (Player_Id, Item). Player_rating depends only on Player_Id. What is its highest normal form?
items.explanation: The table has separate, single-valued cells, but Player_rating depends on only part of the key. This prevents 2NF.

references.label: Week 5 normalization, p. 24
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 5 - Normalization of Database Table  28 Oct 26.pdf

items.question: Player_rating depends only on Player_Id, but Quantity depends on the entire key. Which design removes the partial dependency without losing either fact?

options.text: Player(Player_Id, Player_rating) and Inventory(Player_Id, Item, Quantity)

items.explanation: Player_rating moves to the Player table because it depends only on Player_Id. Quantity stays with the player–item pair.

references.label: Week 5 normalization, p. 25
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 5 - Normalization of Database Table  28 Oct 26.pdf

items.question: Player_Id determines Player_Skill_level, which determines Player_rating. What kind of dependency links Player_Id to Player_rating through Player_Skill_level?

options.text: Full dependency on a composite key

items.explanation: Player_Id determines the numeric skill level, and that level determines the rating label. The rating therefore depends on Player_Id indirectly. Beginner can correspond to more than one numeric skill level; the reverse dependency is not assumed.

references.label: Week 5 normalization, p. 29
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 5 - Normalization of Database Table  28 Oct 26.pdf

context.title: Player example — numeric skill levels and rating labels

items.question: Each player has one skill level, and each skill level determines the rating. Which design removes that transitive dependency while retaining the link?

options.text: Player(Player_Id) and Skill_Level(Player_Skill_level, Player_rating) with no link
Keep all three attributes together in Player

items.explanation: The player keeps their skill level. The rating is stored with that skill level in a separate table.
